text: You just took a huge gulp of a frozen slushie, and now your forehead is screaming.
That ice cold slush just smacked the roof of your mouth.
Right above it run tiny blood vessels that keep your head warm.
The cold makes them squeeze tight, really fast.
Then they snap wide open and blood rushes back in.
That sudden rush sets off a big nerve in your face.
But your brain gets mixed up about where the signal came from.
So it blames your forehead, even though the cold hit your mouth.
To stop it, press your tongue to the roof of your mouth, or sip something warm.
It usually fades in just a few seconds.
Subscribe, because that's what really causes brain freeze.
